head.name: @fzlt/core/drive
head.lead: Vehicle feel on a heightfield, for diorama racing and trail games. One small, fixed-step model for two wheels (a dirt bike) and four (a Jeep, a truck, a buggy, a car): throttle, brake (and reverse), steering that tightens less at speed, grip and drift (the tyres hold a sideways slide only up to grip, a handbrake input lets the rear go), a spring and damper per wheel so the body pitches, rolls, squats and dives with the ground under each wheel, airtime off a lip, and a landing that is judged: a bike that lands nose or tail too far off the slope, or a car that rolls past crashRoll, crashes. - The ground is anything with sample(x, z, out) (out = [height, nx, ny, nz], returns a surface kind): @fzlt/core/terrain is one, and its painted kinds can change the grip (surfaces). - Deterministic: the same inputs from the same start give the same path, bit for bit. The model uses only + − × ÷, square roots and its own polynomial sine and arctangent (the builtins may differ in the last bit between browsers), so two players replaying the same inputs agree. - Suspension: each wheel samples the ground on its own and has its own spring (stiffness or hz, progressive), damper (damping compressing, rebound extending), travel and a bump stop; the body heaves, pitches and rolls on the sum of the spring loads with its own inertia, so a big drop compresses the springs, rebounds and settles (a long-travel buggy: travel 0.5 or more, soft and progressive, more rebound than compression damping). - Outputs for drawing: pos and rot (diorama's order: [roll, yaw, pitch]) for the body, per wheel comp (how far its spring is pushed in) and press (the same, 0..1 of the travel), spin (radians) and contact, bodyPitch and bodyRoll (the lean on the springs), stroke (the most any spring is in: 1 is the bump stop), the front wheels' steerAngle, and dust (0..1: how hard the tyres throw dirt, spray or sand) for an emitter. - Drift: the handbrake input lets the rear go (the grip drops to drift, the tail swings out by swing, the slide is held under slide radians and counter-steer catches it; letting go hands recover of the sideways speed back as forward speed). drift (0..1) says how hard it is drifting right now, slide the body's angle to its travel, chain the drift score so far (∫ drift dt); a chain that ends banks as drive:drift (v: its score; b: 1 when a crash or a spin-out broke it). spinOut(rate, secs) spins it round with no control for a moment. - Contact between vehicles: touch(a, b, opts) (or touchAll(list, opts), every pair in order) pushes two hulls apart (a box from hull [half length, half width], or a circle: one radius) by their mass and bounces their velocities along the contact normal; onHit(a, b, hit) gets the impulse in hit (touchHit: [impulse, nx, nz, depth, x, z], the normal from a to b), so a game can spin out a drifting car it rams. - chase(cam, target, opts, dt) eases a diorama camera behind and above anything with pos and yaw (cosmetic: it uses the builtin maths; pass snap for reduced motion). - Rollback: state is every byte the model carries from step to step (one buffer); save(dst) and load(src) copy it out and back, so a game can rewind and replay a car bit for bit. Zero allocation per step, also with several vehicles in one process (typed arrays; locals; one class for every vehicle, its model in module functions, so a loop over cars keeps one call target). Speeds are world units per second, angles radians.
